title: Microsoft Purview Information Protection: File Labeler and File Viewer for macOS
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates and macOS capabilities match Microsoft's notice and the roadmap. The publishing path, PowerShell call and general licensing statements are supported, and searches found no documentation resolving the narrowly stated macOS-specific gaps.

claims.claim: The Windows File Labeler applies sensitivity labels and encryption using File Explorer.
claims.quote: Information protection file labeler | Used to apply sensitivity labels and encryption using File Explorer.

claims.claim: The Windows information protection Viewer opens encrypted files.
claims.quote: Information protection viewer | Used to view files that are encrypted.

claims.claim: The cited information protection client Learn page describes a Windows-only client.
claims.quote: This client runs on Windows only and replaces the Azure Information Protection (AIP) unified labeling client.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no page describing the macOS File Labeler and File Viewer at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview Information Protection File Labeler File Viewer macOS download system requirements sign in admin block install. Opened information-protection-client; reviewed SDK and client search results, which describe Windows clients or SDKs, not these macOS apps.

claims.claim: Advanced label-based protection is an endpoint DLP setting.
claims.quote: When you configure users for the endpoint data loss prevention setting Advanced label-based protection for all files on devices and use the information protection client

claims.claim: Without the Windows advanced setting, labelling and encrypting files other than Office and PDF changes their file name extension.
claims.quote: When users label and encrypt these files with the information protection client and without this setting for advanced label-based protection: The encrypted file changes its file name extension and becomes read-only

claims.claim: Those Windows encrypted files without the advanced setting open in the information protection Viewer.
claims.quote: can no longer be opened by apps that support the original file name extension. Instead, the file opens in the Microsoft Purview Information Protection viewer.

claims.claim: The Windows advanced setting lets labelled, encrypted files other than Office and PDF retain their extension on the device.
claims.quote: When a user selects a sensitivity label that applies encryption, the file name extension now doesn't change. As a result, there's no change to the user workflow because they can continue to view and edit the file in their standard application.

claims.claim: Access to protected files still depends on permissions in the label's protection.
claims.quote: Control access to content by using encryption for emails, meeting invites, and documents to prevent unauthorized people from accessing this data. You can also choose which users or groups have permissions to perform which actions and for how long.

claims.claim: The sensitivity labels overview requires users applying labels to sign in with their Microsoft 365 work or school account.
claims.quote: To apply sensitivity labels, users must be signed in with their Microsoft 365 work or school account.

claims.claim: The specific sign-in method for the macOS clients is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "macOS" "File Labeler" sign in; Microsoft Purview Information Protection File Labeler File Viewer macOS download system requirements sign in admin block install. Opened sensitivity-labels and information-protection-client; results gave no macOS client sign-in method.

claims.claim: The notice describes user-driven labelling of selected files rather than autonomous activity.
claims.quote: Users will be able to apply labels and protection to single files, or multiple files. Need to work with files, selecting a folder will not show the option.

claims.claim: Windows users can access the File Labeler through a file or folder right-click, unlike the stated macOS folder exception.
claims.quote: Windows computers with monitor resolutions of 800x600 and lower can't fully display the file labeler dialog box when you right-click a file or folder in File Explorer.

claims.quote: Searched: "macOS" "File Labeler" admin enable disable block client installation. Opened information-protection-client; reviewed Intune Gatekeeper and device restrictions results, which describe general device restrictions, not these clients' installation eligibility.

claims.claim: No separate switch to allow or block the macOS clients is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "macOS" "File Labeler" admin enable disable block client installation. Opened information-protection-client, create-sensitivity-labels and Set-LabelPolicy; results gave general device restrictions and label policies, not a separate macOS client switch.

claims.claim: Label publishing policies determine which sensitivity labels are available to which users and groups in the tenant.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.claim: The stated Microsoft Purview portal path reaches label selection and Add in the publishing policy wizard.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. On the Label policies page, select Publish label. On the Choose sensitivity labels to publish page, select the Choose sensitivity labels to publish link. Select the labels ... and then select Add.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AddLabels <label names> adds the named labels to an existing policy.
claims.quote: Set-LabelPolicy [-Identity] <PolicyIdParameter> [-AddLabels <MultiValuedProperty>]. The AddLabels parameter specifies the sensitivity labels that you want to add to the policy. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the label. For example: Name

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Using Set-LabelPolicy requires assigned Microsoft Purview permissions.
claims.quote: To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions. For more information, see Permissions in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal.
